html:
On 6 March 1957 the British colony of the Gold Coast became the independent state of Ghana, the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence from European rule. It took its name from the medieval empire of Ghana.

The road there was short. After riots in Accra in 1948, Kwame Nkrumah founded the Convention People's Party in 1949 and called for "self-government now". Jailed for organising strikes, he won the 1951 election from his cell and was released to lead the government. Six years later he led the country to freedom.

At midnight Nkrumah told the crowd that Ghana's independence meant nothing unless it was linked to the liberation of the whole of Africa. Ghana became a centre of Pan-Africanism, hosting African leaders and exiles. Its example helped speed decolonisation across the continent: seventeen countries became independent in the Year of Africa, 1960.
sum: On 6 March 1957 the British colony of the Gold Coast became the independent state of Ghana, the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence from European rule. It took its name from the medieval empire of Ghana.
